component.name: Kernel Updater for CachyOS on Debian

description.p: Kernel Updater for CachyOS on Debian is an independent, unofficial GTK4 and Libadwaita utility that automates the discovery, compilation, installation, and verification of CachyOS kernels on Debian-based systems. (Not affiliated with or endorsed by the CachyOS or Debian projects.)

Through a guided three-step workflow, users can upgrade to performance-tuned kernels with BORE scheduler optimizations, automatic DKMS rebuilds, fallback kernel retention, and cryptographic MOK Secure Boot signing.

ul.li: Automated Kernel Discovery: Queries upstream CachyOS releases and matches optimal CPU microarchitectures (x86-64-v3 and v4)
Guided 1-2-3 Workflow: Step-by-step verification, pre-installation checks, and automated GRUB configuration
Secure Boot Integration: Automatic Machine Owner Key (MOK) signing for proprietary modules (NVIDIA, Wi-Fi, VirtualBox)
Fallback & Rollback Protection: Retains proven stable kernels to guarantee a bootable system
Containerized Build Isolation: Compiles and packages deb images inside isolated container environments

description.p: Version 1.2.0 UI/UX, Kernel, Podman, and UEFI Release:

ul.li: Redesigned UI around a clean 3-tab Libadwaita AdwViewStack (Update & Build, Secure Boot, Kernels & Logs) with progressive disclosure, symbolic icons, and instant non-blocking startup
Hardened UEFI MOK password handling using 0600 temporary --pass-file passing instead of command-line arguments
Added sbverify pre-check before sbsign to prevent duplicate PE/COFF signatures, /boot free-space check, version-matched linux-headers installation, and systemd-boot fallback
Cached Podman/Docker image verification and added Debian Trixie/Sid container base detection
Removed sched-ext (SCX) userspace BPF scheduler integration and bundled SCX packages to focus on native CachyOS BORE and EEVDF kernel schedulers
Restored full DEBUG_INFO_NONE debug symbol stripping when Strip Debug Symbols is enabled, significantly reducing disk footprint and compile times
Optimized kernel configuration sanitization by batching all scripts/config flags into a single execution
Audited and refactored codebase to remove duplicated dpkg status parsing, redundant MOK helper handlers, and dormant code

Added automatic Debian vs. Ubuntu host OS detection (/run/host/etc/os-release and /etc/os-release) to dynamically select debian:bookworm-slim or ubuntu:24.04 container builders and matching kernel localversions
Aligned application display name, README, and AppStream metadata with Flathub trademark and non-affiliation policies
Updated GNOME Flatpak runtime to version 51 and added automated release-flathub.sh publisher script
Standardized canonical Flatpak and Freedesktop Application ID to io.github.Antux912012.debian-cachy-os-kernel-updater
Updated AppStream catalog, desktop entry, and icon branding under the io.github.Antux912012 namespace
Rebuilt Debian (.deb) and Flatpak (.flatpak) bundles inside the dedicated Podman container environment
Added official application screenshots and AppStream catalog metadata for GNOME Software Center, KDE Discover, and Bazaar
Updated GitHub project documentation and visual walkthrough gallery
Rebuilt Debian (.deb) and standalone Flatpak (.flatpak) packages inside isolated Podman build environment
Fixed UEFI Secure Boot detection inside Flatpak via direct kernel efivars inspection and host mokutil bridging
Added Flatpak-to-host execution bridge (flatpak-spawn --host) so dependency checks, kernel downloads, compilation, installation, MOK signing, and rollbacks work seamlessly in Flatpak
Staged sign-kernel.sh and Containerfile in shared ~/.config/cachy-kernel-updater path accessible across Flatpak and host namespaces
Switched kernel source and config downloads to streaming requests with progress reporting and batched scripts/config sanitization
Fixed missing Wi-Fi and Bluetooth drivers during kernel compilation (localmodconfig driver trimming)
Enforced comprehensive Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AF_ALG/crypto driver safety baselines (Intel, Realtek, Qualcomm/Atheros, MediaTek, Broadcom, BT_HIDP, BT_HCIUART, CMAC, AES, SHA)
Seeded host lsmod module list so streamline_config never drops dormant or unassociated wireless/Bluetooth controllers
Added hardware detection reporting for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth adapters
Updated APT repository and packaging metadata
New vibrant modern CachyOS emblem logo and cohesive teal & crimson branding
Guided 1-2-3 step workflow with safe cross-system defaults
Enhanced UEFI Secure Boot signing pipeline with co-located MOK certificates
Official Debian package (.deb) and standalone Flatpak distribution
